name: Gorgias
tagline: The Shopify-native helpdesk born from a Chrome extension, priced by ticket volume instead of seats, with an AI agent that can actually issue refunds.
tldr: Gorgias is an ecommerce-focused helpdesk that started as a Chrome extension for email templates and pivoted hard into Shopify support after its founders noticed 70% of early users were store support agents — Shopify's Premier Partner for CX status and 40% of Shopify's top 1,500 merchants using it reflect how deep that focus goes.

Pricing is ticket-based, not seat-based: Starter $10/mo (50 tickets), Basic $60/mo (300 tickets), Pro $360/mo (2,000 tickets), Advanced $900/mo (5,000 tickets), each roughly 15-17% cheaper billed annually, with unlimited agents on every plan and per-ticket overage fees beyond the included volume.

AI Agent is billed separately per resolution ($1.00 monthly billing, $0.90 annual) on top of the ticket-tier price, and is explicitly documented as Shopify-only — Gorgias's own docs state AI Agent is not supported on BigCommerce, Magento, or WooCommerce stores.

The Shopify integration is the real differentiator: full order history, shipping status, and lifetime value in the ticket sidebar, with one-click refunds, cancellations, and shipping edits — a materially deeper commerce integration than most helpdesks in this category ship natively.

Reviews split sharply by platform in a way worth taking seriously: strong 4.6/5 averages on both G2 and Capterra, against a starkly lower Trustpilot rating driven substantially by billing disputes — including one documented case of roughly $14,000 in unexpected AI automation fees on top of an existing annual contract.

Best for Shopify-native ecommerce brands with real order-support volume who want deep commerce data inside the ticket — not for WooCommerce/Magento/BigCommerce stores wanting AI parity with Shopify, or teams that need tight, predictable monthly costs.
keyFeatures: AI Agent — an autonomous, action-taking agent that resolves tickets and can issue refunds, cancel orders, and edit shipping details directly, not just draft replies
Native Shopify integration surfacing order history, shipping status, and customer lifetime value directly in the ticket, with one-click refund/cancel/edit actions
BigCommerce integration with comparable order-management actions (refunds, duplicates); WooCommerce and Magento integrations are read-only with no AI Agent support
Macros — reusable response templates that can be chained with rules to auto-tag, auto-assign, or trigger a CSAT survey on ticket close
Revenue statistics that attribute sales to support interactions — sales per day, sales per agent, and tickets converted, filterable by store, channel, and timeframe
Unified ticket inbox across email, live chat, SMS, phone, Instagram, Facebook, and TikTok with collision detection to prevent duplicate agent replies
A dedicated Statistics API for building custom dashboards and BI integrations beyond the built-in reporting suite
Native, one-way HubSpot integration (pulls CRM data into Gorgias) plus Klaviyo and Loop Returns integrations built specifically for ecommerce workflows

companyInfo.founded: 2015 in Paris by Romain Lapeyre and Alex Plugaru, originally a Chrome extension for templated email responses before pivoting to ecommerce helpdesk after discovering 70% of early users were store support agents
companyInfo.hq: San Francisco, California, USA, with additional offices in New York, Charlotte, Toronto, Buenos Aires, Paris, Lisbon, and Sydney
companyInfo.funding: $100M+ raised to date; valued at $530M in a May 2024 Series C round

faq.question: Does Gorgias charge per agent seat?
faq.answer: No — unlike most competitors in this category, Gorgias prices by monthly ticket volume, not by the number of agents. Every plan (Starter through Advanced) includes unlimited users; you're buying ticket capacity, and going over your plan's included ticket count triggers a per-ticket overage fee ($0.40 on Starter/Basic, $0.36 on Pro/Advanced) rather than a hard cutoff.

faq.question: How is Gorgias's AI Agent priced, and does it work on every ecommerce platform?
faq.answer: AI Agent is billed per resolution — $1.00 on monthly billing, $0.90 if billed annually — stacked on top of your ticket-tier plan price. Critically, it's Shopify-only: Gorgias's own documentation states AI Agent is not supported on BigCommerce, Magento, or WooCommerce stores, so non-Shopify merchants get the helpdesk but not the flagship AI capability.

faq.question: What is Gorgias's real AI resolution rate?
faq.answer: Gorgias markets up to 60-80% automation, but independently reported real-world deployments vary widely — from around 26% at some brands to 56%+ at others, depending heavily on setup quality and how much a merchant invests in tuning macros and knowledge sources. Treat the higher published figures as a ceiling under strong conditions, not a typical result, since no independent audit of the vendor's number was found.

faq.question: Can Gorgias's AI actually process a refund, or does it just draft a reply?
faq.answer: On Shopify specifically, it can act: documented capabilities include issuing refunds, canceling orders, and editing shipping details directly, not just suggesting a response for a human to send. Gorgias's own documentation on how AI Agent works describes a second-model confidence check — a generated reply must clear a confidence threshold and be grounded in your knowledge sources or it doesn't get sent, with the conversation instead handed to a human agent.

faq.question: Why do Gorgias's review scores look so different across platforms?
faq.answer: G2 and Capterra both show strong averages around 4.6/5, largely driven by ease-of-use and Shopify-integration praise. Trustpilot's average sits considerably lower, and the negative reviews there skew heavily toward billing disputes — unexpected charges, trial-period confusion, and refund refusals — rather than product-capability complaints. That's a meaningful split worth reading both sides of before signing an annual contract.

faq.question: Is Gorgias good for WooCommerce or Magento stores, not just Shopify?
faq.answer: It integrates with both, but at a materially lower tier of functionality. WooCommerce and Magento integrations are documented as read-only — agents can see order context but must go into the platform's own admin panel to process refunds, cancellations, or edits — and AI Agent isn't supported on either at all. If you're not on Shopify or BigCommerce, budget for a meaningfully more manual workflow.

pricingBreakdown: Gorgias's ticket-based, seat-unlimited pricing is a genuine structural advantage for larger support teams — a 15-agent team pays the same $360/mo on Pro as a 3-agent team handling the same ticket volume, where per-seat competitors like Zendesk or LiveChat would charge multiples more as headcount grows. The tradeoff is that your bill now tracks volume instead of headcount, which reviewers describe as fine at a steady state and stressful during a spike: a busy sales month can push you well past your ticket allowance at $0.36-$0.40 per overage ticket, and AI Agent's $1.00-per-resolution fee (a fully automated resolution counts as both a ticket and a resolution) stacks on top of that. The most serious documented example of this risk is a brand on the Advanced plan reporting roughly $14,000 in AI automation fees in addition to an existing ~$13,500/year contract after turning AI Agent on — a genuinely large, specific number that should make any merchant model their expected resolution volume carefully before enabling it at scale. Against Help Scout's $0.75/resolution or Intercom's $0.99/resolution, Gorgias's $1.00 (or $0.90 annual) sits at the higher end of per-resolution AI pricing in this category, and it's worth noting that non-Shopify merchants pay for a ticket-tier plan but can't access AI Agent at all, since it's explicitly unsupported on BigCommerce, Magento, and WooCommerce.

capabilities.note: This is the actual product, and it's genuinely deep: full order history, shipping status, and customer lifetime value directly in the ticket, with one-click refunds, cancellations, and shipping edits. It's a materially more capable commerce integration than the Shopify apps offered by general-purpose helpdesks in this category, and it's the reason 40% of Shopify's top 1,500 merchants reportedly use Gorgias.

Genuinely agentic — it can act on an order, not just describe one — with a documented two-stage hallucination guard (grounding plus a confidence-threshold check) that hands off to a human rather than guessing. The hard boundary to know before buying: this capability is Shopify-only. BigCommerce, Magento, and WooCommerce merchants get the helpdesk but not this flagship feature.

A distinctive, genuinely uncommon feature in this category: Gorgias tracks sales attributable to support interactions — sales per day, sales per agent, tickets converted — filterable by store and channel. For a commerce-focused team trying to justify a support budget as a revenue driver rather than a cost center, this is a real differentiator most helpdesks don't offer natively.

Meaningfully weaker than the marketing suggests. WooCommerce and Magento integrations are read-only — agents see order context but must switch to the platform's own admin to actually do anything about it — and neither supports AI Agent at all. If you're not on Shopify or BigCommerce, budget for a materially more manual workflow than Gorgias's Shopify-focused case studies imply.

Worth treating as its own capability area given how often it comes up in reviews. Ticket-based, seat-unlimited pricing is genuinely good value for larger teams at steady volume, but the combination of per-ticket overage charges and per-resolution AI fees means a busy month or an AI rollout can produce a real billing surprise — including one documented case of roughly $14,000 in unexpected AI fees on top of an existing contract.

verdict: Gorgias's origin story explains its strength and its limitation in the same breath: it started as a Chrome extension, found its real market in Shopify support agents, and has spent a decade building the deepest Shopify-native helpdesk integration in this category — genuine order data, real refund and cancellation actions, and revenue-attribution reporting that most competitors simply don't offer. The AI Agent extends that same depth: it's genuinely agentic on Shopify, with a documented two-stage hallucination guard that would rather hand off to a human than send an ungrounded reply. The catch, and it's a hard one, is that all of that AI capability stops at Shopify's edge — BigCommerce, Magento, and WooCommerce merchants get a materially less capable, mostly read-only version of the same product, with no AI Agent at all. Pricing follows an unusual and genuinely good structural idea — unlimited agents, pay for ticket volume instead of seats — but the real-world execution of that idea has produced specific, well-documented billing shocks, most strikingly a merchant reporting roughly $14,000 in unexpected AI fees stacked on an existing annual contract. That's not a vague 'pricing could be clearer' complaint; it's a concrete number that should make anyone turning on AI Agent at scale model their expected resolution volume first. The review record itself tells this story in miniature: strong 4.6/5 averages on G2 and Capterra sit against a noticeably rougher Trustpilot record dominated by billing disputes rather than product complaints. My honest read: if you're a Shopify brand with real support volume and you're disciplined about monitoring AI usage against your contract, Gorgias's commerce depth is hard to match. If you're on WooCommerce or Magento, or you need predictable, capped monthly costs more than commerce-specific depth, look elsewhere first.
